newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA INVESTIGATES INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY THEFT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA INVESTIGATES INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY THEFT.

text.p: Bulgaria, strongly criticised by western countries of abusing intellectual property rights, started investigating compact discs producers in the country, the interior ministry said on Friday.

The music industry has urged Bulgaria to act against five CD plants which are estimated to supply approximately one in eight of all illegal copies on the world CD blackmarket, which it says are destabilising the industry and costing it $100 million a year.

EU External Relations commissioner Hans van den Broek, who visited Sofia earlier this week, urged tougher measures to protect intellectual property rights in view of Bulgaria's commitments as a member of the World Trade Organisation.
"Today the Interior Ministry launched the first raid, named Pirates, on the territory of the whole country in search of illegal production of compact discs," a ministry statement said.

Police officers have made an unexpected checks of CDs producing firms in Sofia and in the towns of Botevgrad, Veliko Tarnovo and Stara Zagora, the statement said, adding that producers' lines and storages had been inspected.
As a result of the investigation police have confiscated some 2,000 CDs of CHLS Holding and Unison CDM, which have been without an identification code, the statement said.
Another 6,000 CDs will be confiscated under suspicion that they are pirates production, the statement said.
Since November an identification code engraved on compact discs to identify the producer has been introduced in Bulgaria.
Intellectual piracy has flourished in Bulgaria with the liberalisation of its markets since the fall of its communist rule in 1989.
The IFPI, representing a $40 billion international recording industry, said Bulgaria was now second only to China in the export of pirate CDs, producing an estimated 15 million discs a year.
